metadata.title: Left translates of a square integrable function on the Heisenberg group

nodes.name: shift-invariant subspace
nodes.statement: A closed subspace $V\subset L^{2}(\mathbb{R})$ is called shift-invariant if $f\in V\Longrightarrow \tau_{k}f\in V$ for any $k\in \mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n$
nodes.statement: The Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n$ is a nilpotent Lie group whose underlying manifold is $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}$, where the group operation is defined by $(x,y,t)(x^{\prime},y^{\prime},t^{\prime})=(x+x^{\prime},y+y^{\prime},t+t^{\prime}+\dfrac{1}{2}(x^{\prime}.y-y^{\prime}.x))$ and the Haar measure is the Lebesgue measure $\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}y\mathrm{d}t$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.statement_short: The nilpotent Lie group $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ with the skew-symmetric twisting in the $t$-coordinate and Lebesgue Haar measure.
differentia: the group operation is defined by $(x,y,t)(x^{\prime},y^{\prime},t^{\prime})=(x+x^{\prime},y+y^{\prime},t+t^{\prime}+\dfrac{1}{2}(x^{\prime}.y-y^{\prime}.x))$
the Haar measure is the Lebesgue measure $\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}y\mathrm{d}t$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}$

nodes.name: the standard lattice is a discrete subgroup of $\mathbb{H}^{n}$
nodes.statement: Now it is clear that $\{(2k,l,m):k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n},m\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ is a discrete subgroup of $\mathbb{H}^{n}$.

nodes.name: Stone-von Neumann theorem
nodes.statement: By Stone-von Neumann theorem, every infinite dimensional irreducible unitary representation on the Heisenberg group is unitarily equivalent to the representation $\pi_{\lambda}, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}^{\star}$, where $\pi_{\lambda}$ is defined by \begin{eqnarray*} \pi_{\lambda}(x,y,t)\varphi(\xi)=e^{2\pi i\lambda t}e^{2\pi i\lambda(x.\xi+\frac{1}{2}x.y)}\varphi(\xi+y), \end{eqnarray*} where $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$.
nodes.statement_short: Every infinite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation of $\mathbb{H}^n$ is unitarily equivalent to some $\pi_\lambda$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^\star$.
assumptions: every infinite dimensional irreducible unitary representation on the Heisenberg group
conclusions: is unitarily equivalent to the representation $\pi_{\lambda}, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}^{\star}$

nodes.name: group Fourier transform on $\mathbb{H}^n$
nodes.statement: The group Fourier transform on $\mathbb{H}^n$ is defined to be $$\widehat{f}(\lambda)=\int\limits_{\mathbb{H}^n}f(x,y,t)\pi_\lambda(x,y,t)dxdydt$$ for $f\in L^{1}(\mathbb{H}^n)$. More explicitly, $\widehat{f}(\lambda)$ is the bounded operator acting on $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ (i.e., $\widehat{f}(\lambda)\in \mathcal{B}(L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n}))$) given by $\widehat{f}(\lambda)\varphi=\ds\int\limits_{\mathbb{H}^n}f(x,y,t)\pi_\lambda(x,y,t)\varphi dxdy dt$, where the integral is a Bochner integral taking values in the Hilbert space $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ .
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat{f}(\lambda)$ is the operator-valued integral of $f$ against $\pi_\lambda$, a bounded operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$.
differentia: the integral is a Bochner integral taking values in the Hilbert space $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$

nodes.name: operator-norm bound for $\widehat{f}(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: \|\widehat{f}(\lambda)\|_{\mathcal{B}}\leq \|f\|_{L^{1}(\mathbb{H}^{n})}.

nodes.name: partial Fourier transform $f^{\lambda}$ and $W_{\lambda}(f)$
nodes.statement: Define $f^\lambda(x,y)=\ds\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}}f(x,y,t)e^{2\pi i\lambda t}dt$ to be the inverse Fourier transform of $f$ in the $t$-variable. Thus $\widehat{f}(\lambda)=\ds\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}f^\lambda(x,y)\pi_\lambda(x,y,0)dxdy$. One can write $\widehat{f}(\lambda)=W_\lambda(f^\lambda)$, where $W_{\lambda}(f)$ is given by $$W_\lambda(f)=\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}f(x,y)\pi_\lambda(x,y,0)dxdy,$$ for $f\in L^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$.
nodes.statement_short: $f^\lambda$ is the inverse Fourier transform in $t$, and $\widehat{f}(\lambda)=W_\lambda(f^\lambda)$ factors the group Fourier transform through $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$.

nodes.name: convolution on $\mathbb{H}^{n}$
nodes.statement: for $f,g\in L^{1}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$, the convolution of $f$ and $g$ on $\mathbb{H}^{n}$ is defined to be \begin{eqnarray*} (f*g)(z,t)=\int\limits_{\mathbb{H}^{n}}f((z,t)(w,s)^{-1})g(w,s)dwds. \end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: twisted convolution
nodes.statement: For $f,g\in L^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$, the twisted convolution of $f$ and $g$ is defined to be \begin{eqnarray*} (f\times g)(z)=\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}} f(z-w)g(w)e^{\pi i Im (z.\overline{w})}dw. \end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: twisted convolution corresponds to operator multiplication
nodes.statement: If we define $f^{\#}(z,t)=e^{-2\pi it}f(z)$, then one can show that $f^{\#}* g^{\#}=(f\times g)^{\#}$. Further, for $f,g\in L^{1}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$, one has $\widehat{f*g}(\lambda)=\widehat{f}(\lambda)\widehat{g}(\lambda),~\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{\star} $, as in the case of Euclidean Fourier transform. This leads to $W(f\times g)= W(f) W(g)$
nodes.statement_short: Lifting by $f^{\#}(z,t)=e^{-2\pi it}f(z)$ turns twisted convolution into group convolution, and both are multiplicative under the transform: $W(f\times g)=W(f)W(g)$.

nodes.name: Weyl transform $W(f)$
nodes.statement: $$W(f)=\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}f(x,y)\pi(x,y)dxdy,$$ called the Weyl transform of $f\in L^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$, by taking $\lambda=1$ in $W_{\lambda}(f)$ and by writing $\pi (x,y)=\pi_{1}(x,y,0)$.
nodes.statement_short: The Weyl transform is $W_\lambda$ at $\lambda=1$, integrating $f$ against $\pi(x,y)=\pi_1(x,y,0)$.

nodes.name: lattice in $\mathbb{H}^{n}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathscr{L}$ be a discrete subgroup of the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^{n}$ such that $\mathbb{H}^{n}/\mathscr{L}$ is compact. In other words, $\mathscr{L}$ is a lattice in $\mathbb{H}^{n}$.
nodes.genus: a discrete subgroup of the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^{n}$

nodes.name: principal shift-invariant space $V(\varphi)$ on $\mathbb{H}^{n}$
nodes.statement: For $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$, the principal shift-invariant space, $V(\varphi)$, is defined to be $\overline{span}\{{L_{l}\varphi:l\in\mathscr{L}}\}$, where $L_{l}\varphi(X)=\varphi(l^{-1}.X),~X\in\mathbb{H}^{n}$. However, for the sake of computational convenience the standard lattice $\{(2k,l,m):k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n},m\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ is taken in place of $\mathscr{L}$. Hence for $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n}),~V(\varphi)$ is taken to be the closed linear span of the collection $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}, m\in\mathbb{Z}\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $V(\varphi)$ is the closed span of the left translates $L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi$ over the standard lattice.
nodes.genus: the closed linear span of the collection $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}, m\in\mathbb{Z}\}$
differentia: the standard lattice $\{(2k,l,m):k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n},m\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ is taken in place of $\mathscr{L}$

nodes.name: twisted translation $T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi$
nodes.statement: For $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n}), (k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}$, we define the twisted translation of $\varphi$, denoted by $T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi$, as $$T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi (x,y)= e^{\pi i(x.l-y.k)}\varphi (x-k,y-l),~(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}.$$

nodes.name: twisted shift-invariant space $V^{t}(\varphi)$
nodes.statement: Using this definition, the twisted shift-invariant space of $\varphi$, denoted by $V^{t}(\varphi)$, is defined to be the closed linear span of $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi: (k,l)\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}\}$ in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$.
nodes.definiendum: twisted shift-invariant space of $\varphi$, denoted by $V^{t}(\varphi)$
nodes.genus: the closed linear span of $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi: (k,l)\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}\}$ in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$

nodes.name: explicit formula for the Weyl transform
nodes.statement: The Weyl transform of a function $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ can be explicitly written as \begin{eqnarray*} W(f)\varphi (\xi)=\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}} f(x,y)e^{2\pi i(x.\xi+\frac{1}{2}x.y)}\varphi(\xi+y)dxdy,~~ \varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{n}),~~ z=x+iy, \end{eqnarray*} which maps $L^{1}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ into the space of bounded operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{n})$, denoted by $\mathcal{B}(L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{n}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Integral formula for $W(f)\varphi(\xi)$, showing $W$ maps $L^1(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ into $\mathcal{B}(L^2(\mathbb{R}^n))$.

nodes.name: kernel $K_{f}(\xi,\eta)$ of the Weyl transform
nodes.statement: The Weyl transform $W(f)$ is an integral operator with kernel $K_{f}(\xi,\eta)$ given by \begin{eqnarray*} \int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}f(x,\eta-\xi)e^{i\pi x\cdot(\xi+\eta)}dx. \end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: extension of $W$ to tempered distributions
nodes.statement: This map $W$ can be uniquely extended to a bijection from the class of tempered distributions $S^{\prime}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ onto the space of continuous linear maps from $S(\mathbb {R}^{n})$ into $S^{\prime}(\mathbb {R}^{n})$. If $f\in L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$, then $W(f)\in\mathcal{B}_{2}(L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{n}))$, the space of Hilbert-Schmidt operators on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$.
nodes.statement_short: $W$ extends uniquely to a bijection on tempered distributions, and sends $L^2(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ into the Hilbert-Schmidt class.
conclusions: This map $W$ can be uniquely extended to a bijection from the class of tempered distributions $S^{\prime}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ onto the space of continuous linear maps from $S(\mathbb {R}^{n})$ into $S^{\prime}(\mathbb {R}^{n})$
$W(f)\in\mathcal{B}_{2}(L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{n}))$, the space of Hilbert-Schmidt operators on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$

nodes.name: Plancherel identity for the Weyl transform
nodes.statement: \langle W(f), W(g)\rangle_{\mathcal{B}_{2}}=\langle f,g\rangle_{L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})}=\langle K_{f},K_{g}\rangle_{L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})}.
nodes.statement_short: Weyl transform and its kernel both preserve the $L^2$ inner product.

nodes.name: Plancherel theorem for the group Fourier transform on $\mathbb{H}^{n}$
nodes.statement: The group Fourier transform is an isometric isomorphism of $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ onto $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{\star},\mathcal{B}_{2};\\d\mu)$ , where $\mathcal{B}_{2}$ denotes the space of Hilbert-Schmidt operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ and $d\mu(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{n}d\lambda$.
nodes.statement_short: The group Fourier transform is a unitary map of $L^2(\mathbb{H}^n)$ onto the Hilbert-Schmidt-valued space with measure $|\lambda|^n d\lambda$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{B}_{2}$ denotes the space of Hilbert-Schmidt operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$
conclusions: The group Fourier transform is an isometric isomorphism of $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ onto $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{\star},\mathcal{B}_{2};\\d\mu)$

nodes.name: Plancherel formula on $\mathbb{H}^{n}$ in terms of $W_{\lambda}$
nodes.statement: \langle f, g\rangle&=& \int\limits_{\mathbb{R}}\langle \widehat{f}(\lambda),\widehat{g}(\lambda)\rangle_{\mathcal{B}_{2}} |\lambda|^{n}d\lambda =\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}} \langle W_{\lambda}(f^{\lambda}), W_{\lambda}(g^{\lambda})\rangle_{\mathcal{B}_{2}} |\lambda|^{n}d\lambda.
nodes.statement_short: The $L^2(\mathbb{H}^n)$ inner product is the $|\lambda|^n d\lambda$-integral of Hilbert-Schmidt inner products of $W_\lambda(f^\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Bessel sequence
nodes.statement: A sequence $\{f_{k}:{k \in\mathbb {Z}}\}$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is called a Bessel sequence for $\mathcal{H}$ if there exists a constant $B > 0$ such that \begin{eqnarray*} \sum \limits_{k \in\mathbb {Z}}|\langle f,f_{k} \rangle |^{2}\leq B\|f\|^{2},\hspace{4mm}\forall f\in \mathcal{H}. \end{eqnarray*}
differentia: there exists a constant $B > 0$ such that $\sum \limits_{k \in\mathbb {Z}}|\langle f,f_{k} \rangle |^{2}\leq B\|f\|^{2},\hspace{4mm}\forall f\in \mathcal{H}$

nodes.name: frame
nodes.statement: A sequence $\{f_{k}:{k \in\mathbb {Z}}\}$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is called a frame for $\mathcal{H}$ if there exist two constants $A,B > 0$ such that \begin{eqnarray*} A\|f\|^{2}\leq\ds\sum \limits_{k \in\mathbb {Z}}|\langle f,f_{k} \rangle |^{2}\leq B\|f\|^{2},\hspace{4mm}\forall f\in \mathcal{H}. \end{eqnarray*}
differentia: there exist two constants $A,B > 0$ such that $A\|f\|^{2}\leq\ds\sum \limits_{k \in\mathbb {Z}}|\langle f,f_{k} \rangle |^{2}\leq B\|f\|^{2},\hspace{4mm}\forall f\in \mathcal{H}$

nodes.name: $\ell^{2}$-linear dependence and independence
nodes.statement: A sequence $\{f_{k}:{k \in\mathbb {Z}}\}$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is said to be $\ell^{2}$-linearly dependent if there exists a non-zero sequence $\{c_{k}\}\in\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $\sum\limits_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}c_{k}f_{k}=0$. If the sequence $\{c_{k}\}$ is not $\ell^{2}$-linearly dependent, then it is said to be $\ell^{2}$-linearly independent.
nodes.statement_short: A sequence is $\ell^2$-linearly dependent if some non-zero $\ell^2$ coefficient sequence annihilates it, and $\ell^2$-linearly independent otherwise.
differentia: there exists a non-zero sequence $\{c_{k}\}\in\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $\sum\limits_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}c_{k}f_{k}=0$

nodes.name: kernel of the Weyl transform of a twisted translate
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi \in L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$. Then the kernel of the Weyl transform of $T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi$ satisfies the following relation. \begin{eqnarray} K_{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi}(\xi,\eta)=e^{\pi i (2\xi+l).k}K_{\varphi}(\xi+l,\eta). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: $K_{T^{t}_{(k,l)}\varphi}$ is a unimodular exponential factor times $K_\varphi$ shifted by $l$ in the first variable.

nodes.name: the function $w_{\varphi}$
nodes.statement: For $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$, the function $w_{\varphi}$ is defined as follows. \begin{eqnarray*} w_{\varphi}(\xi)=\sum\limits_{m\in \mathbb{Z}^{n}}\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}| K_{\varphi}(\xi+m,\eta)|^{2} d\eta,\hspace{4 mm} \xi\in \mathbb{R}^{n}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: $w_\varphi(\xi)$ periodizes the squared $L^2$-mass of the kernel $K_\varphi$ over integer shifts of $\xi$.

nodes.name: condition C for $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$
nodes.statement: A function $\varphi \in L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ is said to satisfy ``condition C'' if \begin{eqnarray*} \sum\limits_{m\in\mathbb {Z}^{n}}\int\limits_{\mathbb {R}^{n}}K_{\varphi}(\xi+m,\eta)\overline{K_{\varphi}(\xi+m+l,\eta)}d\eta=0 ~~ a.e.~ \xi\in \mathbb {T}^{n}, ~~{\rm for~ all} ~~l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}\setminus \{0\}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: The periodized cross-correlations of $K_\varphi$ at all non-zero integer shifts $l$ vanish a.e.

nodes.name: characterization of Bessel sequences of twisted translates
nodes.statement: If $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb {Z}^{2n}\}$ is a Bessel sequence in $L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ with bound B, then $w_{\varphi}(\xi)\leq B$ a.e. $\xi\in\mathbb {T}^{n}$. Conversely, suppose $w_{\varphi}(\xi)\leq B$ a.e. $\xi\in\mathbb {T}^{n}$. If, in addition $\varphi$ satisfies condition C, then $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb {Z}^{2n}\}$ is a Bessel sequence in $L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ with bound B.
nodes.statement_short: Bessel implies $w_\varphi\le B$; conversely $w_\varphi\le B$ plus condition C implies Bessel with the same bound.
assumptions: If $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb {Z}^{2n}\}$ is a Bessel sequence in $L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ with bound B
If, in addition $\varphi$ satisfies condition C
conclusions: $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb {Z}^{2n}\}$ is a Bessel sequence in $L^{2}(\mathbb {R}^{2n})$ with bound B

nodes.name: the map $J_{\varphi}$ on $A^{t}(\varphi)$
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C. Suppose $A^{t}(\varphi)={\rm span}\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi\\:{(k,l)\in \mathbb{Z}^{2n}}\}$ and $V^{t}(\varphi)=\overline{A^{t}(\varphi)}$. Consider $f\in A^{t}(\varphi)~i.e., f= \sum\limits_{(k^{\prime},l^{\prime})\in\mathcal{F}}c_{k',l'}T_{(k',l')}^{t}\varphi$, where $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite set. Define $\rho(\xi)=\{\fontdimen16\textfont2=5pt \rho_{l^{\prime}}(\xi)\}_{l^{\prime}\in\mathbb {Z}^{n}}$ for $\xi\in\mathbb {T}^{n}$, where $\fontdimen16\textfont2=5pt \rho_{l^{\prime}}(\xi)=\sum\limits_{k^{\prime}}c_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime}}e^{\pi i(2\xi+l^{\prime}).k^{\prime}}$. Define $J_{\varphi}(f)=\rho$.
nodes.statement_short: $J_\varphi$ sends a finite twisted-translate combination to the vector of trigonometric polynomials $\rho_{l'}(\xi)=\sum_{k'}c_{k',l'}e^{\pi i(2\xi+l').k'}$.

nodes.name: $J_{\varphi}$ evaluated on a twisted translate
nodes.statement: In particular, taking $f=T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi$, one has \begin{eqnarray} J_{\varphi}(T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi)(\xi)=(\dotsc ,0,\dotsc ,0,e^{\pi il.k}e^{2\pi ik.\xi},0,\dotsc ,0,\dotsc) \end{eqnarray} with $e^{\pi il.k}e^{2\pi ik.\xi}$ in the $l$th position a.e. $\xi\in\mathbb{T}^{n}$.
nodes.statement_short: $J_\varphi(T^{t}_{(k,l)}\varphi)$ is the sequence with $e^{\pi il.k}e^{2\pi ik.\xi}$ in the $l$th slot and zeros elsewhere.

nodes.name: $J_{\varphi}$ is an isometric isomorphism on $V^{t}(\varphi)$
nodes.statement: The map $J_{\varphi}$ initially defined on $A^{t}(\varphi)$ can be extended to an isometric isomorphism between $V^{t}(\varphi)$ and $L^{2}(\mathbb {T}^{n},\ell^{2}(\mathbb {Z}^{n}),w_{\varphi})$.
conclusions: can be extended to an isometric isomorphism between $V^{t}(\varphi)$ and $L^{2}(\mathbb {T}^{n},\ell^{2}(\mathbb {Z}^{n}),w_{\varphi})$

nodes.name: kernel characterization of membership in $V^{t}(\varphi)$
nodes.statement: Moreover, it was proved that $f\in V^{t}(\varphi)$ if and only if \begin{eqnarray} K_{f}(\xi,\eta)=\ds\sum\limits_{l^{\prime}\in\mathbb {Z}^{n}}\fontdimen16\textfont2=5pt \rho_{l^{\prime}}(\xi)K_{\varphi}(\xi+l',\eta), \end{eqnarray} where $\rho(\xi)= \{\fontdimen16\textfont2=5pt \rho_{l^{\prime}}(\xi)\}_{l^{\prime}\in\mathbb {Z}^{n}}$ and $\rho\in L^{2}(\mathbb {T}^{n},\ell^{2}(\mathbb {Z}^{n}),w_{\varphi})$.
nodes.statement_short: $f\in V^{t}(\varphi)$ exactly when $K_f$ is the $\rho$-weighted superposition of integer shifts of $K_\varphi$ with $\rho\in L^{2}(\mathbb{T}^{n},\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z}^{n}),w_{\varphi})$.

nodes.name: norm identity for finite combinations of twisted translates
nodes.statement: Let $\{c_{k,l}:(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ be a finite sequence and $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C. Then \begin{eqnarray} \bigg\|\sum\limits_{(k,l)\in\mathcal{F}}c_{k,l}T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi\bigg\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})}^{2}=\sum\limits_{l} \int\limits_{\mathbb {T}^{n}}\bigg|\sum\limits_{k}c_{k,l}e^{\pi il.k}e^{2\pi ik.\xi}\bigg|^{2} w_{\varphi}(\xi)d\xi, \end{eqnarray} where $\mathcal{F}$ denotes a finite set.
nodes.statement_short: Under condition C the $L^2$ norm of a finite twisted-translate sum equals a $w_\varphi$-weighted sum of $L^2(\mathbb{T}^n)$ norms of its trigonometric polynomials.
assumptions: $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C

nodes.name: the function $G_{k,l}^{\varphi}$
nodes.statement: For $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ and $(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}$, the function $G_{k,l}^{\varphi}$ is defined as follows. \begin{eqnarray} G_{k,l}^{\varphi}(\lambda)=\sum\limits_{r\in\mathbb{Z}}\langle\widehat{\varphi} (\lambda+r),\widehat{L_{(2k,l,0)}\varphi}(\lambda+r)\rangle_{\mathcal{B}_{2}} |\lambda+r|^{n},~\lambda\in (0,1]. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: $G^{\varphi}_{k,l}(\lambda)$ periodizes the Hilbert-Schmidt inner products of $\widehat\varphi$ against $\widehat{L_{(2k,l,0)}\varphi}$ over $\lambda+\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: condition C for $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$
nodes.statement: A function $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ is said to satisfy ``condition C'' if $G_{k,l}^{\varphi}(\lambda)=0$ a.e. $\lambda\in (0,1],~\forall~(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\setminus\{(0,0)\}$.

nodes.name: condition C reduces to vanishing of Fourier coefficients
nodes.statement: In order to show that a function $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ satisfies condition C, it is enough to show that all the Fourier coefficients of $G_{k,l}^{\varphi}$ vanish when $(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\setminus \{(0,0)\}$. But \begin{eqnarray} \widehat{G_{k,l}^{\varphi}}(m)=\int\limits_{0}^{1} G_{k,l}^{\varphi}(\lambda) e^{-2\pi im\lambda}d\lambda =\langle\varphi, L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle_{L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})}. \end{eqnarray} Thus it is enough to show that $\langle\varphi, L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle=0,~\forall~m\in\mathbb{Z}$, whenever $(k,l)\neq (0,0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Checking condition C amounts to showing $\langle\varphi,L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle=0$ for all $m$ whenever $(k,l)\neq(0,0)$.

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients of $G_{k,l}^{\varphi}$
nodes.statement: \widehat{G_{k,l}^{\varphi}}(m)=\int\limits_{0}^{1} G_{k,l}^{\varphi}(\lambda) e^{-2\pi im\lambda}d\lambda =\langle\varphi, L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle_{L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})}.
nodes.statement_short: The $m$th Fourier coefficient of $G^{\varphi}_{k,l}$ equals $\langle\varphi,L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle$.

nodes.name: Example 1: $\varphi=\chi_{[0,2]}\otimes\chi_{[0,1]}\otimes h$ satisfies condition C
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi(x,y,t)=\chi_{[0,2]}(x)\chi_{[0,1]}(y)h(t)$, where $h$ is an arbitrary function in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R})$. Then \begin{eqnarray*} L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi (x,y,t) &=&\varphi(x-2k,y-l,t-m+\frac{1}{2}(2ky-xl))\\ &=& \chi_{[0,2]}(x-2k)\chi_{[0,1]}(y-l) h(t-m+ky-\frac{l}{2}x)\\ &=& \chi_{[2k,2k+2]}(x)\chi_{[l,l+1]}(y) h(t-m+ky-\frac{l}{2}x). \end{eqnarray*} Since for $(k,l)\neq (0,0), [0,2]\times [0,1]~\bigcap~ [2k,2k+2]\times [l,l+1]=\emptyset,$ it follows that $\langle \varphi, L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle=0,~\forall~ m\in\mathbb{Z}$. Then from \eqref{3pr6}, we get $\widehat{G_{k,l}^{\varphi}}(m)=0,~\forall~ m\in\mathbb{Z}$ whenever $(k,l)\neq (0,0)$. Thus $\varphi$ satisfies condition C.
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness of the translated supports forces all inner products $\langle\varphi,L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi\rangle$ to vanish, so condition C holds.

nodes.name: characterization of orthonormal systems of left translates
nodes.statement: In \cite{ra}, we have proved the theorem that $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is an orthonormal system in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ if and only if $G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda)=1$ a.e. $\lambda\in (0,1]$ and $\varphi$ satisfies condition C.
nodes.statement_short: Left translates of $\varphi$ form an orthonormal system iff $G^{\varphi}_{0,0}\equiv 1$ a.e. and $\varphi$ satisfies condition C.
conclusions: is an orthonormal system in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ if and only if $G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda)=1$ a.e. $\lambda\in (0,1]$ and $\varphi$ satisfies condition C

nodes.name: condition C does not imply orthonormality
nodes.statement: Thus it is meaningful to give an example of a function $\varphi$ which satisfies condition C but $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is not an orthonormal system. This is illustrated in Example 2 and Example 3.

nodes.name: Example 2: Gaussian $h(t)=e^{-t^{2}}$ gives condition C without orthonormality
nodes.statement: We take $h(t)=e^{-t^{2}}, t\in\mathbb{R},$ in Example 1. For this function $h$, the correspond-ing $\varphi$ satisfies $\langle\varphi, L_{(0,0,1)}\varphi\rangle\neq 0$. Hence $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ does not form an orthonormal system in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H})$.

nodes.name: Example 3: general $h$ with non-vanishing autocorrelation at $1$
nodes.statement: Instead of $e^{-t^{2}}$, one can take $e^{-|t|}$ or in general any $h\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R})$ for which $\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}}h(t)h(t-1)dt\neq 0$. Then $\langle\varphi, L_{(0,0,1)}\varphi\rangle\neq 0$.

nodes.name: Example 4: separable $\varphi=f\otimes g\otimes h$ with translation-disjoint supports
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi(x,y,t)=f(x)g(y)h(t)$, where $supp~f\bigcap supp~\tau_{2k}f=\emptyset,~\forall~k\neq 0$ and $supp~g\bigcap supp~\tau_{l}g=\emptyset,~\forall~l\neq 0,~h\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R})$. Then the same proof discussed in Example 1 can be used to show that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C. Again as an example, we can take \begin{eqnarray*} f(x)&=\left\{ \begin{array}{l l} e^{-\frac{1}{x(2-x)}},& \quad \text{$0<x<2$,}\\ 0, & \quad \text{otherwise,} \end{array}\right. \end{eqnarray*} and \begin{eqnarray*} g(x)&=\left\{ \begin{array}{l l} e^{-\frac{1}{x(1-x)}},& \quad \text{$0<x<1$,}\\ 0, & \quad \text{otherwise,} \end{array}\right. \end{eqnarray*} and $h(t)=e^{-t^{2}},~t\in\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.statement_short: Any product $f(x)g(y)h(t)$ whose factors have supports disjoint from their relevant translates satisfies condition C; explicit smooth bump factors are given.

nodes.name: Example 5: $\varphi=\chi_{[0,3]}\otimes\chi_{[0,1]}\otimes h$ fails condition C
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi(x,y,t)=\chi_{[0,3]}(x)\chi_{[0,1]}(y)h(t)$, where $h$ is an arbitrary function in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R})$. Then it can be shown that \begin{eqnarray*} \langle\varphi, L_{(2,0,0)}\varphi\rangle =\int\limits_{0}^{1}\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}} h(t)\overline{h(t+y)}dtdy. \end{eqnarray*} Choose $h$ in such a way that the above integral is non-zero. For example, we can take $h(t)=sinct,~t\in\mathbb{R}$. Then \begin{eqnarray*} \langle\varphi, L_{(2,0,0)}\varphi\rangle =\int\limits_{0}^{1}\frac{sin\pi y}{\pi y}dy >0. \end{eqnarray*} Thus from \eqref{3pr6}, we have $\widehat{G_{1,0}^{\varphi}}(0)\neq 0$, showing that $\varphi$ does not satisfy condition C.
nodes.statement_short: With overlapping support of width $3$ and $h=\mathrm{sinc}$, $\langle\varphi,L_{(2,0,0)}\varphi\rangle>0$, so $\widehat{G^{\varphi}_{1,0}}(0)\neq0$ and condition C fails.

nodes.name: Example 6: general separable $\varphi$ failing condition C
nodes.statement: More generally, let $\varphi(x,y,t)=f(x)g(y)h(t)$, where the value of both the integrals $\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}} f(x)\overline{f(x-2)}dx$ and $\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}}\int\limits_{\mathbb{R}}|g(y)|^{2}h(t)\overline{h(t+y)}dt dy$ are non-zero. Since $\langle\varphi, L_{(2,0,0)}\varphi\rangle\neq 0$, $\varphi$ does not satisfy condition C. For example, we can take $f(x)=e^{-|x|},~x\in\mathbb{R},~ h(t)=sinct,~t\in\mathbb{R}$ and \begin{eqnarray*} g(y)&=\left\{ \begin{array}{l l} \frac{1}{n+1},& \quad \text{$y\in [2n,2n+1],~n=0,1,2,\dotsc $,}\\ 0, & \quad \text{otherwise.} \end{array}\right. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Any separable $\varphi$ whose two displayed integrals are non-zero has $\langle\varphi,L_{(2,0,0)}\varphi\rangle\neq0$ and hence fails condition C.

nodes.name: $G_{k,l}^{\varphi}$ is finite almost everywhere
nodes.statement: Let $m=0$ in \eqref{3pr6}. Then we have \begin{eqnarray*} \int\limits_{0}^{1}G_{k,l}^{\varphi}(\lambda)d\lambda=\langle\varphi, L_{(2k,l,0)}\varphi\rangle<\infty, \end{eqnarray*} which shows that the function $G_{k,l}^{\varphi}(\lambda)$, defined in \eqref{3peq18}, is finite a.e. $\lambda\in (0,1]$.
nodes.statement_short: Taking $m=0$ in the Fourier-coefficient identity shows $G^{\varphi}_{k,l}$ is integrable, hence finite a.e. on $(0,1]$.

nodes.name: characterization of Bessel sequences of left translates on $\mathbb{H}^{n}$
nodes.statement: If $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is a Bessel sequence in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ with bound B, then $G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda)\leq B$ a.e. $\lambda\in(0,1]$. Conversely, suppose $G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda)\leq B$ a.e. $\lambda\in(0,1]$. If, in addition $\varphi$ satisfies condition C, then $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is a Bessel sequence in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ with bound B.
nodes.statement_short: Bessel implies $G^{\varphi}_{0,0}\le B$; conversely $G^{\varphi}_{0,0}\le B$ plus condition C gives Bessel with bound $B$.
assumptions: If $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is a Bessel sequence in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ with bound B
If, in addition $\varphi$ satisfies condition C
conclusions: $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is a Bessel sequence in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ with bound B

nodes.name: the map $J_{\varphi}$ on $A(\varphi)$
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C. Suppose $A(\varphi)=$ span $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$. Then $V(\varphi)=\overline{A(\varphi)}$. Let $f\in A(\varphi)$ i.e., $f=\sum\limits_{(k^{\prime},l^{\prime},m^{\prime})\in\mathcal{F}} c_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime},m^{\prime}}L_{(2k^{\prime},l^{\prime},m^{\prime})}\varphi$, where $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite set. Define $\rho(\lambda)=\fontdimen16\textfont2=5pt \{\rho_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime}}(\lambda)\}_ {(k^{\prime},l^{\prime})}$ for $\lambda\in (0,1]$, where \begin{eqnarray} \fontdimen16\textfont2=5pt \rho_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime}}(\lambda)=\sum\limits_{m^{\prime}} c_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime},m^{\prime}}e^{2\pi im^{\prime}\lambda}. \end{eqnarray} Define $J_{\varphi}(f)=\rho$.
nodes.statement_short: On $\mathbb{H}^n$, $J_\varphi$ sends a finite left-translate combination to $\rho=\{\rho_{k',l'}\}$ with $\rho_{k',l'}(\lambda)=\sum_{m'}c_{k',l',m'}e^{2\pi im'\lambda}$.

nodes.name: $J_{\varphi}$ is an isometric isomorphism on $V(\varphi)$
nodes.statement: The map $J_{\varphi}$ initially defined on $A(\varphi)$ can be extended to an isometric isomorphism between $V(\varphi)$ and $L^{2}((0,1],\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z}^{2n}),G_{0,0}^{\varphi})$.
nodes.origin_citation: Radha & Adhikari (arXiv:1711.06902), proved here for completeness
conclusions: can be extended to an isometric isomorphism between $V(\varphi)$ and $L^{2}((0,1],\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z}^{2n}),G_{0,0}^{\varphi})$

nodes.name: canonical dual
nodes.statement: An element $\varphi\in\mathcal{H}$ is said to be a canonical dual to the system $\{f_{k}:k\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ if $\langle f_{k},\varphi\rangle=\delta_{k,0},~\forall~k\in\mathbb{Z}$. In case, if $f_{k}$ is generated from a single function $f$ by some transformation, then $\varphi$ is called a canonical dual to $f$.

nodes.name: Besselian sequence
nodes.statement: A sequence $\{f_{k}:{k \in\mathbb {Z}}\}$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is said to be Besselian if $\sum\limits_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}c_{k}f_{k}$ is convergent implies $\{c_{k}\}\in\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z})$.

nodes.name: Hilbertian sequence
nodes.statement: A sequence $\{f_{k}:{k \in\mathbb {Z}}\}$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is said to be Hilbertian if $\{c_{k}\}\in\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z})$ implies $\sum\limits_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}c_{k}f_{k}$ converges.

nodes.name: multiplier lemma: $sL^{1}\subset L^{1}$ forces $s\in L^{\infty}$
nodes.statement: Suppose a measurable non-negative function $s$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ satisfies $sm\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$, whenever $m\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$, then $s\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$.
nodes.statement_short: A non-negative measurable $s$ that multiplies $L^1(\mathbb{T}^n)$ into itself is essentially bounded.
assumptions: Suppose a measurable non-negative function $s$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ satisfies $sm\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$, whenever $m\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$

nodes.name: existence of a non-zero function supported in $A$ with uniformly bounded partial sums
nodes.statement: For every measurable subset $A\subset\mathbb{T}^{n}$ with $\lambda{(A)}> 0$, $\lambda{(A^{c})}> 0$, there exists non-zero $f\in L^{2}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item supp~$f\subset A$; \item there exists $M> 0$ such that $\|S_{n}(f)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^{n})}\leq M$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, where $S_{n}(f)$ denotes the nth partial sum of the Fourier series of $f$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: On any measurable $A\subset\mathbb{T}^n$ of positive measure and positive complement there is a non-zero $f\in L^2$ supported in $A$ whose Fourier partial sums are uniformly bounded.
conclusions: there exists non-zero $f\in L^{2}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$ such that

Then, using \eqref{3pr1}, we have \begin{eqnarray*} \|f\|^{2}=\sum\limits_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime}}\int\limits_{0}^{1} |\rho_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime}}(\lambda)|^{2} G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda) d\lambda &=&\int\limits_{0}^{1} \|\rho(\lambda)\|_{\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z}^{2n})}^{2}G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda) d\lambda\\ &=&\|\rho\|_{L^{2}((0,1],\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z}^{2n}),G_{0,0}^{\varphi})}^{2}. \end{eqnarray*} Hence $J(\varphi)$ is an isometry. Using density argument this isometry can be extended to the whole of $V(\varphi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude $\|f\|^{2}=\|\rho\|^{2}_{L^{2}((0,1],\ell^{2},G^{\varphi}_{0,0})}$, so $J_\varphi$ is an isometry, extended to $V(\varphi)$ by density.

nodes.name: characterization of membership in $V(\varphi)$
nodes.statement: Moreover from \eqref{3pr5}, we have $f\in V(\varphi)$ if and only if \begin{eqnarray} \widehat{f}(\lambda)=\sum\limits_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime}\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}} \fontdimen16\textfont2=5pt \rho_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime}}(\lambda)\widehat{L_{(2k^{\prime},l^{\prime}, 0)}\varphi}(\lambda), \end{eqnarray} where $\rho(\lambda)=\{\fontdimen16\textfont2=5pt \rho_{k^{\prime},l^{\prime}}(\lambda)\}_ {(k^{\prime},l^{\prime})\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}}$ and $\rho\in L^{2}((0,1],\ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z}^{2n}),G_{0,0}^{\varphi})$.
nodes.statement_short: Read off that $f\in V(\varphi)$ iff $\widehat{f}$ is the $\rho$-weighted superposition of $\widehat{L_{(2k',l',0)}\varphi}$ with $\rho$ in the weighted $L^2$ space.

nodes.name: canonical dual in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ for twisted translates
nodes.statement: Accordingly, we say that a function $\tilde{\varphi}\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ is said to be a canonical dual to a function $\varphi$ in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ if $\langle T_{(k,l)}^{t}\tilde{\varphi},\varphi\rangle=\delta_{(k,l),(0,0)}$ holds for every $k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}$.
nodes.section: 3 Canonical dual in twisted shift-invariant spaces
nodes.definiendum: canonical dual to a function $\varphi$ in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1: existence of the canonical dual in $V^{t}(\varphi)$
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C. Then there exists a canonical dual $\tilde{\varphi}$ to $\varphi$ that belongs to $V^{t}(\varphi)$ if and only if $\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$. Moreover, in this case, $K_{\tilde{\varphi}}(\xi,\eta)=\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}(\xi)} K_{\varphi}(\xi, \eta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Under condition C, a canonical dual in $V^{t}(\varphi)$ exists iff $1/w_\varphi\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$, and then $K_{\tilde\varphi}=K_\varphi/w_\varphi$.
nodes.section: 3 Canonical dual in twisted shift-invariant spaces
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C
conclusions: there exists a canonical dual $\tilde{\varphi}$ to $\varphi$ that belongs to $V^{t}(\varphi)$ if and only if $\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$

nodes.name: Theorem 4.1: $w_{\varphi}>0$ implies $\ell^{2}$-linear independence
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C. Suppose $w_{\varphi}(\xi)> 0$ a.e. $\xi\in\mathbb{T}^{n}$. Then $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in \mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is $\ell^{2}$- linearly independent.
nodes.section: 4 Non-redundancy property of Twisted translates in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C

nodes.name: Theorem 4.2: converse under the Bessel assumption
nodes.statement: Suppose $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in \mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is a Bessel sequence with bound B that is $\ell^{2}$-linearly independent. Then $w_{\varphi}(\xi)> 0$ a.e. $\xi\in\mathbb{T}^{n}$.
nodes.section: 4 Non-redundancy property of Twisted translates in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$
assumptions: Suppose $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in \mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is a Bessel sequence with bound B that is $\ell^{2}$-linearly independent

nodes.name: Theorem 4.3: converse without the Bessel assumption
nodes.statement: Let $0\neq\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$. If $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in \mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is $\ell^{2}$-linearly independent, then $w_{\varphi}(\xi)> 0$ a.e. $\xi\in\mathbb{T}^{n}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\ell^{2}$-linear independence of the twisted translates of any non-zero $\varphi$ already forces $w_\varphi>0$ a.e.
nodes.section: 4 Non-redundancy property of Twisted translates in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$

nodes.name: Theorem 5.1: Hilbertian implies $\|w_{\varphi}\|_{\infty}<\infty$
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C. Assume that $\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$. If $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in \mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is Hilbertian, then $||w_{\varphi}||_{\infty}<\infty$.
nodes.section: 5 Twisted translates as Besselian and Hilbertian sequences in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C

nodes.name: Theorem 5.2: $\|w_{\varphi}\|_{\infty}<\infty$ implies Hilbertian
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$. Assume that $\|w_{\varphi}\|_{\infty}<\infty$. Then $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is Hilbertian.
nodes.section: 5 Twisted translates as Besselian and Hilbertian sequences in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$

nodes.name: Theorem 5.3: Hilbertian $\Leftrightarrow$ $\|w_{\varphi}\|_{\infty}<\infty$ $\Leftrightarrow$ Bessel
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$. Then the following are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item [(a)] $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is Hilbertian. \item [(b)] $\|w_{\varphi}\|_{\infty}<\infty$. \item [(c)] $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is a Bessel sequence. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Under condition C and $1/w_\varphi\in L^{1}$, the twisted translates are Hilbertian iff $w_\varphi$ is essentially bounded iff they form a Bessel sequence.
nodes.section: 5 Twisted translates as Besselian and Hilbertian sequences in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$

nodes.name: Theorem 5.4: existence of a canonical dual with Besselian twisted translates
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$. If any one of the equivalent conditions of Theorem \ref{3pth8} is true, then there exists $\tilde{\varphi}\in V^{t}(\varphi)$, canonical dual to $\varphi$ such that $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\tilde{\varphi}:(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is Besselian. Moreover, if $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is Besselian and if for each $\psi\in V^{t}(\varphi)$ there exists a sequence $\{c_{k,l}\}$ such that $\psi=\sum\limits_{k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}}c_{k,l}T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi$, then $\|\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\|_{\infty}<\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Under the equivalent conditions there is a canonical dual $\tilde\varphi\in V^{t}(\varphi)$ whose twisted translates are Besselian; conversely Besselian plus representability forces $\|1/w_\varphi\|_\infty<\infty$.
nodes.section: 5 Twisted translates as Besselian and Hilbertian sequences in $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{w_{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{n})$
If any one of the equivalent conditions of Theorem \ref{3pth8} is true

if $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi:(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is Besselian and if for each $\psi\in V^{t}(\varphi)$ there exists a sequence $\{c_{k,l}\}$ such that $\psi=\sum\limits_{k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}}c_{k,l}T_{(k,l)}^{t}\varphi$
conclusions: there exists $\tilde{\varphi}\in V^{t}(\varphi)$, canonical dual to $\varphi$ such that $\{T_{(k,l)}^{t}\tilde{\varphi}:(k,l)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n}\}$ is Besselian

nodes.name: canonical dual in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ for left translates
nodes.statement: Correspondingly, we say that a function $\tilde{\varphi}\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ is said to be a canonical dual to a function $\varphi$ in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ if $\langle L_{(2k,l,m)}\tilde{\varphi},\varphi\rangle=\delta_{(k,l,m),(0,0,0)}$ holds for every $k,l\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}, m\in\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.definiendum: canonical dual to a function $\varphi$ in $L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$

nodes.name: Theorem 6.1: existence of the canonical dual in $V(\varphi)$ on $\mathbb{H}^{n}$
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C. Then there exists a canonical dual $\tilde{\varphi}$ to $\varphi$ that belongs to $V(\varphi)$ if and only if $\frac{1}{G_{0,0}^{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(0,1]$. Moreover, in this case, $\widehat{\tilde{\varphi}}(\lambda)=\frac{1}{G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda)} \widehat{\varphi}(\lambda)$.
nodes.statement_short: Under condition C, a canonical dual in $V(\varphi)$ exists iff $1/G^{\varphi}_{0,0}\in L^{1}(0,1]$, and then $\widehat{\tilde\varphi}=\widehat\varphi/G^{\varphi}_{0,0}$.
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C
conclusions: there exists a canonical dual $\tilde{\varphi}$ to $\varphi$ that belongs to $V(\varphi)$ if and only if $\frac{1}{G_{0,0}^{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(0,1]$

nodes.name: Theorem 6.2: $G_{0,0}^{\varphi}>0$ implies $\ell^{2}$-linear independence of left translates
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C. If $G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda)>0$ a.e. $\lambda\in (0,1]$, then $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is $\ell^{2}$-linearly independent.
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C

nodes.name: Theorem 6.3: converse on $\mathbb{H}^{n}$ (stated without proof)
nodes.statement: Let $0\neq\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$. Assume that $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is $\ell^{2}$-linearly independent. Then $G_{0,0}^{\varphi}(\lambda)>0$ a.e. $\lambda\in (0,1]$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.4: Hilbertian $\Leftrightarrow$ $\|G_{0,0}^{\varphi}\|_{\infty}<\infty$ $\Leftrightarrow$ Bessel
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{G_{0,0}^{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(0,1]$. Then the following are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item [(a)] $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is Hilbertian. \item [(b)] $\|G_{0,0}^{\varphi}\|_{\infty}<\infty$. \item [(c)] $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is a Bessel sequence. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: The $\mathbb{H}^n$ analogue of the three-way equivalence, with $G^{\varphi}_{0,0}$ in place of $w_\varphi$.
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{G_{0,0}^{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(0,1]$

nodes.name: Theorem 6.5: existence of a dual with Besselian left translates
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{G_{0,0}^{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(0,1]$. If any of the equivalent conditions of the above theorem holds, then there exists $\tilde{\varphi}\in V(\varphi)$ such that $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\tilde{\varphi}:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is Besselian. Moreover, if $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is Besselian and if for each $\psi\in V(\varphi)$, there exists a sequence $\{c_{k,l,m}\}$ such that $\psi=\sum\limits_{(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}}c_{k,l,m}L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi$, then $\|\frac{1}{G_{0,0}^{\varphi}}\|_{\infty}<\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: The $\mathbb{H}^n$ analogue: the equivalent conditions give $\tilde\varphi\in V(\varphi)$ with Besselian left translates, and conversely $\|1/G^{\varphi}_{0,0}\|_\infty<\infty$.
assumptions: Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb{H}^{n})$ be such that $\varphi$ satisfies condition C and $\frac{1}{G_{0,0}^{\varphi}}\in L^{1}(0,1]$
If any of the equivalent conditions of the above theorem holds

if $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is Besselian and if for each $\psi\in V(\varphi)$, there exists a sequence $\{c_{k,l,m}\}$ such that $\psi=\sum\limits_{(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}}c_{k,l,m}L_{(2k,l,m)}\varphi$
conclusions: there exists $\tilde{\varphi}\in V(\varphi)$ such that $\{L_{(2k,l,m)}\tilde{\varphi}:(k,l,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2n+1}\}$ is Besselian
